- [FACT] User inquired about how Columbia University supports entrepreneurship among its students.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Columbia University has a dedicated space called Columbia Startup Lab that provides co-working space, mentoring, workshops, events, and access to resources for student entrepreneurs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Columbia Entrepreneurship Program offers a range of resources and programs to support students in launching their ventures, including courses, workshops, mentorship, funding, and opportunities to pitch to investors.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Columbia Technology Ventures supports the commercialization of inventions and discoveries made by researchers and students at Columbia, offering resources for entrepreneurship training, patent filings, licensing, and funding.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Columbia Business School has a dedicated entrepreneurship center that offers courses, mentoring, networking events, and funding opportunities for student entrepreneurs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Columbia University hosts several entrepreneurship competitions and offers funding opportunities for student startups, including the Columbia Venture Competition, Seed Capital Funding, and the Lang Fund for Entrepreneurship.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Columbia University has a robust ecosystem that supports student entrepreneurship, providing resources, training, network, mentorship, and funding opportunities to transform ideas into successful ventures.
- [USER] User expressed admiration for the information provided, stating, "That's really impressive."
- [USER] User asked if any successful startups have come out of these programs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Venmo, co-founded by Columbia alumni Andrew Kortina and Iqram Magdon-Ismail, was acquired by PayPal for $800 million in 2013.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Warby Parker, co-founded by four Wharton School students, one of whom graduated from Columbia University, is now valued at over $3 billion.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Blue Apron, co-founded by Columbia Business School graduate Matt Salzberg, went public in 2017 and earned $881 million in its IPO.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Harry's, co-founded by Columbia Business School alumnus Jeff Raider, was acquired by Edgewell Personal Care for $1.37 billion in 2020.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These success stories demonstrate the entrepreneurial ecosystem at Columbia University, which provides the right resources and support to help startup ventures grow and succeed.
